subject: The Papyrus · From empty temples to 19 million visitors
html:
The steepest V in the data

In 2020, the temples were nearly empty. Egypt's tourism revenue fell to about $4.4bn, down from a pre-pandemic peak near $13bn in 2019 — a drop of roughly 65–70% in a single year. For a country where tourism feeds foreign currency, jobs, and whole cities, that was a body blow. (Source: worlddata.info.)

Then it came back — and kept going

The recovery didn't just recover; it set records. Arrivals reached 14.9 million in 2023, 15.7 million in 2024, and about 19 million in 2025 — up roughly 21% year on year, and an all-time high. Revenue climbed with it to around $16.7bn in 2025. (Sources: Egypt State Information Service; Central Bank of Egypt via Trading Economics; Al-Ahram.)

Where the honesty lives

Tourism revenue is a place where sources genuinely disagree — receipts versus expenditure, fiscal versus calendar year — so some years carry a range rather than one clean figure. EgyBI's tourism_annual table keeps those caveats in the note field instead of hiding them, because a number you can't source is a number you can't trust. That is the difference between a dashboard and a decision.

Arrivals and revenue by year are both in the table — plot them together and the V-shape draws itself.
